opportunities.title: Post-Grant Academic & Digital Humanities Web-App Staticization
target_users: University libraries and institutional repository managers
opportunities.strongest_alternative: The Endings Project (UVic) + Webrecorder/Browsertrix (WACZ) + Zenodo/Software Heritage
opportunities.strongest_counterevidence: Wren et al. (2017) showed 94% of highly cited scientific resources relocate successfully on their own versus 34% of uncited ones, meaning many disappearing tools lack active demand, and compute-heavy servers cannot be purely staticized.
opportunities.falsifier: Attempt semi-automated staticization/WASM packaging on 20 randomly sampled open-source decaying academic/DH web apps within 48 hours; if fewer than 25% retain core functionality due to heavy backend/DB dependencies, reject broad staticization.

demand.basis: Peer-reviewed studies verify 31% decay across 3,649 bioinformatics web servers and 9.3-year median lifespan across 14,489 scholarly URLs, though direct WTP for a new tool is unverified.

international.basis: Evidence spans 375 international journals and Web of Science citations across NA, EU, and Asia with shared open-science standards.

innovation.basis: Endings Project requires upfront redesign and WACZ captures presentation rather than computation, leaving a plausible retrofit gap.

theme.basis: Anchored in retired academic web services and WebCite's 2023 shutdown, though framed more around scholarly workflows than one iconic dead product.

ai.basis: AI can assist dependency analysis and static/WASM conversion, but much of the pipeline is achievable with deterministic static analysis.

feasibility.basis: A scoped prototype converting a class of open-source academic web apps into static/WACZ bundles is achievable within 7 days using public repositories.

demo.basis: Clear before/after showing a broken legacy research web app running offline in-browser, though requiring brief scholarly context.

sustainability.basis: University libraries and public research funders have established preservation budgets and low legal friction under open licenses.

opportunities.title: Post-Shutdown SaaS & Federated Export Semantic Rehydration
target_users: Product/design teams and SMEs migrating off discontinued SaaS
Fediverse (Mastodon/ActivityPub) users and instance admins facing server shutdowns
Knowledge workers transferring personal/AI work histories across platforms
opportunities.strongest_alternative: Data Transfer Project (DTI) + native competitor importers (Figma, Miro, Notion)
opportunities.strongest_counterevidence: Leading commercial competitors often build free native importers for major shutting-down rivals (e.g., Miro acquiring InVision Freehand), and post-shutdown exports frequently omit internal relational IDs or business logic.
opportunities.falsifier: Inspect 3 real export archives (Mastodon Activity Streams 2.0, Cohost export, and a public SaaS export); if original exports strip foreign-key/thread references so that <50% of relational context is recoverable, reject the space.

demand.basis: Backed by EU Data Act enforcement (Sept 2025), 3,626 stars on DTP, Mastodon's documented post-import limitation, and InVision's permanent data deletion (Dec 2024), though direct WTP for a generic rehydrator is unverified.

international.basis: EU Data Act applies extraterritorially to EU-serving providers, DTI operates globally from NA, and SaaS/Fediverse lock-in affects NA, EU, and Asia alike.

innovation.basis: DTI/DTP focuses on simplified canonical models and Mastodon cannot import exported posts, leaving a concrete post-export relational usability gap.

theme.basis: Meets the gate when anchored to exports from specifically discontinued platforms (e.g., Cohost Jan 2025 or InVision Dec 2024), but risks drifting into generic ETL.

ai.basis: AI is load-bearing for inferring undocumented schemas and relational graphs across heterogeneous export dumps, verifiable against deterministic referential-integrity checks.

feasibility.basis: A working core slice operating on legal real-world export files (e.g., Mastodon Activity Streams 2.0 or public Cohost exports) is achievable within 7 days.

demo.basis: Highly visual under-3-minute before/after: ingesting an unusable flat JSON/ZIP export and restoring an interactive, linked workspace exportable to open formats.

sustainability.basis: Clear B2B compliance and migration revenue path tied to EU Data Act switching mandates (fee ban Jan 2027), with manageable medium legal risk around multi-user data.

opportunities.title: Automated Environment Discovery & Configuration for Institutional Software Emulation
target_users: Museums and national archives operating emulation infrastructure (EaaSI/SPN members)
opportunities.strongest_alternative: EaaSI (Yale/SPN) with manual archivist configuration + Internet Archive Software Collection
opportunities.strongest_counterevidence: The institutional GLAM market is tiny and grant-dependent (Mellon/Sloan/IMLS), and the U.S. Copyright Office's Oct 2024 DMCA §1201 decision rejected remote research access to preserved games, capping institutional ROI.
opportunities.falsifier: Benchmark automated manual/header parsing plus sandbox boot-testing on 15 public/shareware DOS/Win3.1/Mac68k titles; if automated boot success is <50% or does not outperform default DOSBox/IA presets, reject.

demand.basis: Primary Stanford BDPL/EaaSI case study confirms 2 full days of manual trial-and-error for a single 1985 title, but the addressable institutional buyer base is narrow.

international.basis: Verified across NA and EU via SPN, EaaSI, DPC, and IIPC networks; direct Asian emulation deployment evidence was not found in this round.

innovation.basis: No existing tool automates end-to-end documentation parsing, emulator/OS matrix matching, and sandboxed boot verification for EaaSI workflows.

theme.basis: Directly brings verifiably obsolete operating systems and discontinued software back to life.

ai.basis: AI extracts system requirements from legacy manuals/headers and proposes candidate environments checked by a measurable boot/render oracle.

feasibility.basis: Feasible for 1-2 open emulators (e.g., DOSBox/v86 in browser) within 7 days, but carries material licensing risk around proprietary legacy OS images/ROMs.

demo.basis: Compelling under-3-minute demo: drop a legacy disk image and scanned manual, watch the system infer requirements and boot the software live.

sustainability.basis: Plausible as grant-funded open-source tooling integrated into EaaSI/SPN, but not viable as a standalone commercial product.

opportunities.title: End-of-Life Sunset & Community Handover Governance for Live-Service Platforms
target_users: Open-source server preservation communities (e.g., Pretendo Network)
Indie and mid-size EU game/platform publishers facing upcoming EC EOL code of conduct
Independent community platform operators planning graceful shutdowns
opportunities.strongest_alternative: Post-shutdown clean-room reverse engineering by volunteers (Pretendo Network, Wiimmfi) or manual publisher offline patches
opportunities.strongest_counterevidence: Major publishers strongly oppose EOL obligations due to third-party middleware licensing and liability, and the European Commission explicitly declined mandatory legislation on June 16, 2026.
opportunities.falsifier: Conduct structured interviews with 10 indie game studios or independent platform operators in EU/NA on adopting an EC-aligned EOL handover kit; if >=8/10 refuse even if free due to middleware IP/security liability, reject the publisher-side model.

demand.basis: 1,294,188 validated EU signatures on Stop Destroying Videogames ECI, 170 active Pretendo GitHub repos, and major platform shutdowns (Cohost, Tianya).

international.basis: Direct primary evidence across EU (ECI), NA (Cohost, DMCA §1201), and Asia (Nintendo 3DS/Wii U, Tianya Club China).

innovation.basis: A standardized lightweight EOL handover kit is missing, but the core bottleneck is legal and economic rather than purely technical.

theme.basis: Directly anchored in discontinued online services (Nintendo Network 3DS/Wii U, Cohost) and keeping them operational.

ai.basis: AI is unnecessary for the core problem of IP licensing, architecture decoupling, and EOL governance; adding AI would be decorative.

feasibility.basis: Depends on publisher cooperation not in hand or enters high-risk DRM/EULA reverse-engineering territory if built third-party.

demo.basis: Demonstrating a synthetic client-server sunset handover works technically but relies on synthetic apps rather than real commercial services.

sustainability.basis: High legal risk (DMCA §1201, third-party middleware IP) and no verified payer after publisher support ends.

opportunities.title: Consent-Aware & Sovereign Community Digital Heritage Preservation
target_users: Indigenous and minority cultural heritage stewards (GIDA/CARE-aligned)
Independent community archives preserving shutting-down regional platforms
National libraries operating permission-based private web archiving (e.g., NDL WARP)
opportunities.strongest_alternative: Mukurtu CMS + Webrecorder/WACZ + national selective web archives (NDL WARP, NLK OASIS)
opportunities.strongest_counterevidence: Opt-in consent workflows incur heavy administrative overhead and low coverage, which is why Singapore amended its NLB Act in 2019 to drop prior written consent for .sg domains.
opportunities.falsifier: Survey 15 community archive leads or closing-forum admins offering (a) free public Wayback/WACZ archival vs (b) a consent-and-PII-redacted gated archive requiring 2 hours of setup; if >80% choose (a), reject.

demand.basis: Strong legal and institutional signals (NDL Law exclusions, GDPR Art. 89, Hachette v. IA, GIDA CARE, DPC Bit List), but limited direct evidence of demand for a new tool over Mukurtu/WACZ.

international.basis: Direct primary evidence across Japan (NDL WARP), Korea/Singapore (OASIS/IIPC), EU (GDPR Art. 89), NA (Hachette v. IA), and global Indigenous networks (GIDA).

innovation.basis: Mukurtu handles cultural access controls and WACZ handles web packaging; combining automated PII/consent triage with portable web archives is a moderate gap.

theme.basis: Below the Resurrection gate (>=3): focuses on archival ethics and legal compliance broadly rather than reviving a specific dead technology.

ai.basis: AI helps detect multilingual PII and sensitive entities for GDPR Art. 89 safeguards with human-in-the-loop review, partially replaceable by rules/NER.

feasibility.basis: A consent-tagged WACZ packaging and PII redaction pipeline is feasible within 7 days using open datasets.

demo.basis: Policy- and compliance-oriented value requires domain explanation to resonate with a general hackathon panel.

sustainability.basis: Plausible institutional/NGO grant model with a cleaner legal posture than indiscriminate scraping, though unverified commercially.
